title: A monotone PAGER floor repair must also change the positive-loss formula to match recorded death rates
abstract: We prove a constraint on repairs to a public PAGER fatality probability rule. At source commit 081a55f8, any repair confined to model losses below 0.00099 that preserves the positive-loss formula and risk order at fixed spread can assign at most 0.000043914 probability of at least one death. A reused frozen archive has 109 events with recorded deaths in 6,373 floor reports, a frequency of 0.0171034, or 389 times that bound. Thus a repair cannot meet all three conditions on this sample. We also tested the pinned source functions. Two-element ranges apply the floor, but three-breakpoint ranges do not. This gave inconsistent range representations in all 15 floor cases of a 50-case grid. CDF and quantile helpers also omit the small-loss spread cap. The production loss-model caller uses two-element ranges; we do not show that a public product used the other helpers. A minimal monotone envelope shows why a repair that retains a nonzero risk anchor must also change some positive-loss probabilities. It is a mathematical construction, not a validated forecast. Monotonicity is a design assumption, not a physical law. The outcome check reuses prior data and inherits incomplete death records. The result applies to one public commit, not a verified current operational executable. Code, proof, aggregate results, source hashes, tests and a figure are included.

display.caption: The pinned range rule, the curve with no floor, and an illustrative monotone envelope. Recorded death frequencies exceed the sharp bound for monotone floor-only repairs at three tested thresholds. Wilson intervals assume independent events.
